title: Your phone
subtitle: screen, charger, text, swipe
summary: Name the parts of a phone and talk about texting, calling, taking selfies and saving or deleting photos.

lesson.heading: Parts of a phone
lesson.text: Every smartphone has the same main parts. The **battery** gives the phone power, and you fill it again with a **charger**. You look at the **screen**, you start the phone with the **power button**, and the **camera** takes photos.

examples.text: My **battery** is low. Have you got a **charger**?
Press the **power button** to start your phone.

lesson.heading: Phone words
rows: you use it to fill the battery again
stores the information you need to use your phone
small programs on your phone, e.g. a dictionary or a map

lesson.heading: Using a smartphone
lesson.text: A photo you take of yourself is a **selfie**, and you **post** it online. If nobody answers, you **leave a voicemail**. You can also **text** someone or send them a **message**.

examples.text: Ramesh takes a lot of **selfies** and **posts** them online.
Lisa didn't **answer** her phone, so I left a **voicemail**.
Can you **text** me the address of the restaurant?
I've just got a **message** from Andy. He wants to know if we're going to the party.

lesson.heading: Apps and calls
lesson.text: You **download** an **app** from the Internet onto your phone. When you speak to someone on the phone, you **call** them.

examples.text: You can **download** an **app** with a dictionary to help you when you write in English.
While she was on holiday, Kelly **called** her family every day.

lesson.heading: Locked, unlock and swipe
lesson.text: When your phone is **locked**, you need a **PIN** (a secret number) to **unlock** it. To move from one photo to the next, you **swipe** the screen with your finger.

examples.text: *A:* Can you read that message on my phone, please? *B:* It's **locked**. What's the **PIN**?
You don't need a PIN to **unlock** it. Just **swipe** the screen left to right.

lesson.heading: Save and delete
lesson.text: You **save** the photos you want to keep. When the phone **memory** is **full**, you must **delete** some photos and messages.

examples.text: *A:* I can't **save** any new photos. *B:* Your phone **memory** is **full**.
You need to **delete** some photos and messages.

lesson.text: We text a person and we call a person, but we leave someone a voicemail - not ~~we voicemail someone~~.

exercises.prompt: Maria ___ me last night, but I didn't see her message until this morning.
exercises.explanation: We text someone when we send them a short written message.

exercises.prompt: When your phone's battery is low, you need a ...
exercises.explanation: A charger fills the battery again.

exercises.prompt: Match the things on your phone with what they do.

pairs.right: stores the information you need to use your phone

exercises.prompt: Danny's new phone has a great ___. It takes amazing photos.
exercises.explanation: The camera is the part of the phone that takes photos.

exercises.prompt: What was the last app that you ___?
exercises.explanation: You download an app from the Internet onto your phone.

exercises.prompt: Lucy ___ her sister. They talked about their holiday at the beach.
exercises.explanation: We call someone when we speak to them on the phone.

exercises.prompt: Victor left me a ___. He asked me to call him back.
exercises.explanation: If someone does not answer the phone, you leave a voicemail.

exercises.prompt: I bought a new ___ in France, so that it was cheaper to call and use the Internet.
exercises.explanation: The SIM card stores the information you need to use your phone.

exercises.prompt: *Deepa:* Do I ___ right to see the next photo? *Ireena:* Yes, that's right.
exercises.explanation: You swipe the screen to move from one photo to the next.

exercises.prompt: I didn't delete the photos from the restaurant. I ___ them in a different folder.
exercises.explanation: You save the photos you want to keep.

exercises.statement: Your phone memory is full, so you need to delete some photos and messages.
exercises.explanation: Correct. When the memory is full, you delete things to make space.

exercises.prompt: Is it a part of your phone, or something you do with your phone?
Ask a friend to send you the address of the restaurant.
exercises.answer: Can you text me the address of the restaurant?
